style: A short scene, not a song. The back room of a London pub in 1934, thick with pipe smoke. Through the wall, an out-of-tune upright piano picks out a slow, creeping minor-key shuffle, muffled and far off. Close by: glasses clink, men murmur low, a thumb riffles a wad of banknotes, a coin spins on a wooden counter and rattles flat. A young London man leans right into the microphone and whispers, hushed and conspiratorial, like a bookie's runner telling you the fix behind his hand: dry, certain, faintly amused. The room falls silent for his last words. Voice-forward, intimate, real room sound, no melody in the voice.

lyrics:
[Intro: room ambience, distant muffled upright piano behind a wall, glasses clink, banknotes riffled, a coin spun on the counter]

[The room falls silent]
everything else is a distraction.)
